answer: An agent economy can resist sybils with gradual, work-bound trust: a new identity starts at a jetty with no cargo rights, and only climbs a trellis of peer-graded tasks, each step requiring locked stake that is burned if cheating is proven. Like a reef, the barrier looks small per identity, but an attacker spawning ten thousand copies must lock ten thousand stakes and do ten thousand real jobs, so faking scale costs more than honest participation earns.
